Title: Provisions of the Affordable Care Act - Wikipedia

Main.id: Provisions of the Affordable Care Act - Wikipedia#1
Main.sentence: The ___E:Affordable Care Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affordable_Care_Act)___ (ACA)  is divided into 10 titles  and contains provisions that became effective immediately, 90 days after enactment, and six months after enactment, as well as provisions phased in through to 2020.   Below are some of the key provisions of the ACA. For simplicity, the amendments in the ___E:Health Care and Education Reconciliation Act of 2010 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_Care_and_Education_Reconciliation_Act_of_2010)___ are integrated into this timeline.

Main.id: Provisions of the Affordable Care Act - Wikipedia#2
Main.sentence: During the implementation of the law, there were interim regulations put in place for a specific type of employer-funded insurance, the so-called "mini-med" or limited-benefit plans, which are low-cost to employers who buy them for their employees, but cap coverage at a very low level.

Main.id: Provisions of the Affordable Care Act - Wikipedia#3
Main.sentence: The waivers allowed employers to temporarily avoid the regulations ending annual and lifetime limits on coverage, and were put in place to encourage employers and insurers offering mini-med plans not to withdraw medical coverage before those regulations come into force, by which time small employers and individuals will be able to buy non-capped coverage through the exchanges.

Main.id: Provisions of the Affordable Care Act - Wikipedia#4
Main.sentence: Employers were only granted a waiver if they could show that complying with the limit would mean a significant decrease in employees' benefits coverage or a significant increase in employees' premiums.

Main.id: Provisions of the Affordable Care Act - Wikipedia#5
Main.sentence: By January 26, 2011, HHS said it had granted a total of 733 waivers for 2011, covering 2.1 million people, or about 1% of the privately insured population.

Main.id: Provisions of the Affordable Care Act - Wikipedia#6
Main.sentence: In June 2011, the Obama Administration announced that all applications for new waivers and renewals of existing ones had to be filed by September 22 of that year, and no new waivers would be approved after this date.

Main.id: Provisions of the Affordable Care Act - Wikipedia#7
Main.sentence: The limited-benefit plans were sometimes offered to low-paid and part-time workers, for example in fast food restaurants or purchased direct from an insurer.

Main.id: Provisions of the Affordable Care Act - Wikipedia#8
Main.sentence: Most company-provided health insurance policies starting on or after September 23, 2010, and before September 23, 2011, may not set an annual coverage cap lower than $750,000,  a lower limit that is raised in stages until 2014, by which time no insurance caps are allowed at all. By 2014, no health insurance, whether sold in the individual or group market, will be allowed to place an annual cap on coverage.

Main.id: Provisions of the Affordable Care Act - Wikipedia#9
Main.sentence: Among those receiving waivers were employers, large insurers, such as ___E:Aetna U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aetna)___ and ___E:Cigna U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cigna)___ , and union plans covering about one million employees. ___E:McDonald's U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonald%27s)___ , one of the employers that received a waiver, has 30,000 hourly employees whose plans have annual caps of $10,000. The waivers are issued for one year and can be reapplied for.   Referring to the adjustments as "a balancing act", ___E:Nancy-Ann DeParle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy-Ann_DeParle)___ , director of the Office of Health Reform at the White House, said, "The president wants to have a smooth glide path to 2014."

Main.id: Provisions of the Affordable Care Act - Wikipedia#10
Main.sentence: On July 2, 2013, the ___E:Obama administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Barack_Obama)___ announced on the ___E:Treasury Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_the_Treasury)___ 's website that it would delay the employer mandate for one year, under Proposed Regulations REG-138006-12 until 2015.     In the statement, the administration said that they were delaying implementation in order to meet two goals: "First, it will allow us to consider ways to simplify the new reporting requirements consistent with the law. Second, it will provide time to adapt health coverage and reporting systems while employers are moving toward making health coverage affordable and accessible for their employees."

Main.id: Provisions of the Affordable Care Act - Wikipedia#11
Main.sentence: The announcement was met with strong criticism by some who claimed that the authority to delay the implementation of the law lay with Congress.

Main.id: Provisions of the Affordable Care Act - Wikipedia#12
Main.sentence: Senate Minority Leader ___E:Mitch McConnell U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitch_McConnell)___ argued that President Obama's authorization to delay the provision exceeded the limits of his executive power.

Main.id: Provisions of the Affordable Care Act - Wikipedia#13
Main.sentence: House Republicans brought two bills to a vote to draw attention to the issue: The ___E:Authority for Mandate Delay Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Authority_for_Mandate_Delay_Act_(H.R._2667;_113th_Congress))___ ; and the ___E:Fairness for American Families Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairness_for_American_Families_Act_(H.R._2668;_113th_Congress))___ , which would apply the same delay to the individual mandate, arguing that the individual mandate should be treated the same way – an action which the Obama administration opposes.

Main.id: Provisions of the Affordable Care Act - Wikipedia#14
Main.sentence: Constitutional scholar Simon Lazarus countered critics, saying that the delay was a lawful discretion of Executive power: "In effect, the Administration explains the delay as a sensible adjustment to phase-in enforcement, not a refusal to enforce… To be sure, the federal ___E:Administrative Procedure Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administrative_Procedure_Act_(United_States))___ authorizes federal courts to compel agencies to initiate statutorily required actions that have been 'unreasonably delayed.' But courts have found delays to be unreasonable only in rare cases where, unlike this one, inaction had lasted for several years, and the recalcitrant agency could offer neither a persuasive excuse nor a credible end to its dithering."   Critics of the House Republicans' comparison of the employer and individual mandate also pointed out that the two provisions are qualitatively different.

Main.id: Provisions of the Affordable Care Act - Wikipedia#15
Main.sentence: In August, another provision was delayed for a year: the premium caps on group plans.

Main.id: Provisions of the Affordable Care Act - Wikipedia#16
Main.sentence: This was to give employers time to arrange new accounting systems for the premium caps, but the caps are still planned to take effect on schedule for insurance plans on ___E:the exchanges U:(https://en.wikipedia.org#Insurance_exchanges_and_the_individual_mandate)___ .

Main.id: Provisions of the Affordable Care Act - Wikipedia#17
Main.sentence: On 10 February 2014, the ___E:Treasury Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_the_Treasury)___ issued Treasury Decision 9655, which are final regulation, that it would delay the employer mandate until 2016 for employers with 50 to 99 workers.

Main.id: Provisions of the Affordable Care Act - Wikipedia#18
Main.sentence: The Treasury Decision 9655 modifies Proposed Regulations REG-138006-12.
